(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 empowers

Assertion A is correct as Section 10 empowers the

the Central or State Advisory Board before

questions.question_english:
A contractor supplying security guards to several
Directorate of Education schools in Delhi has his
licence suspended by the licensing officer without
being given an opportunity to show cause. Is this
legally sound?
options_english:
Yes, because the licensing officer possesses
absolute statutory discretionary power to
suspend any licence immediately.

Yes, provided that the registered principal
employer formally requested the immediate
suspension of the licence.

No, because only the jurisdictional High
Court holds the legal authority to suspend a
contractor’s valid licence.

No, Section 14 mandates giving the licence
holder a reasonable opportunity to show
cause.
questions.explanation_english:
No, Section 14 mandates giving the licence
holder a reasonable opportunity to show cause.
Section 14(1) mandates that before revoking or
suspending a licence, the licensing officer must
give the contractor a reasonable opportunity of
showing cause. Action taken without affording
this statutory opportunity violates natural
justice and contravenes express provisions of the
Act.

key_facts:
Correct option (English): No, Section 14 mandates giving the licence
holder a reasonable opportunity to show
cause.

options_hindi: केवल I, II और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the conditions for prohibiting contract
labour under Section 10(2) of the Contract
Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970:
I.
The work is incidental or necessary for the
industry/establishment.
II. The work is of perennial nature.
III. The work is done ordinarily through regular
workmen.
IV. The contractor requests for abolition due to
lack of profit.
Which of the above are statutory considerations
under the Act?
options_english: I, II and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
questions.explanation_english:

Section 10(2) lists statutory considerations:
work necessity, perennial nature, regular worker
practices, and workforce capacity. A contractor’s
request due to lack of profit is not a statutory
ground for prohibiting contract labour under the
Act.

questions.question_english:
Does the definition of “Contractor” under the
Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition)
Act, 1970 include a sub-contractor?
options_english:
No, sub-contractors are treated as separate
entities exempt from the Act.

Yes, provided the sub-contractor works

questions.explanation_english:

produce a given result for an establishment
through contract workers is bound by the same
statutory licensing, welfare, and wage obligations
prescribed under the legislation.

questions.question_english:
A contractor places a new security guard at a
school gate. The guard requests the Principal for
a Service Certificate (Form XV) because he is
resigning. Who is legally responsible for issuing
this certificate?
options_english: The Principal of the school

Identify the committee whose recommendations

abolishing contract labour in India.
options_english: Kothari Commission
Sachar Committee
Second National Commission on Labour
Royal Commission on Labour
questions.explanation_english:
Royal Commission on Labour
The Royal Commission on Labour, reporting in
1931, highlighted the widespread exploitation
inherent in the contract labour system in India.
Its observations and recommendations regarding
working conditions, payment of wages, and job
security formed the foundational groundwork
that eventually led to statutory intervention
and the enactment of the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act in 1970.
